- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to underpredict upward moves; adjust forecast upward by 2–5% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior period), model often overreacts and overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above peak or use moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-period, model lags in recognizing momentum; add 1–3% upward bias in subsequent 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if price is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce forecast by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- When sentiment is positive and price is falling, model often undercorrects; add 1–2% downward bias to prevent overcorrection.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates late-period volatility; increase final 5–7 days’ forecast by 1–3% to account for tail risk.
